item.title: The Visible Strain: A Gentle Squeeze in Private Credit
item.dc:creator: Evan Campbell, CFA
item.description: BDCs provide a rare, regulated window into the opaque world of private credit. Analyzing $65B in assets, we track the shift from cash interest to payment-in-kind (PIK) and the visible lag in defaults. The data reveals a gentle but persistent squeeze. It is proof that high rates are breaking borrowers, just slowly. While not a crash, the system is accommodating stress rather than resolving it.

item.title: The CMBS Window on Private Asset Valuations in Europe
item.dc:creator: Evan Campbell, CFA
item.description: Europe’s 2025 CMBS cohort offers a clear window on private valuations. Using disclosures across €6.9 billion of issuance, we show how appraised marks diverge from rating-agency values, with most deals in a 23% to 34% haircut band and a 29.6% median. The piece explains why this gap emerges, where it may persist in private markets with thin price discovery, and how investors should treat reported cushions and re-underwrite cash flows.

item.title: Where the Capital Went: Allocation Tilt, New Drivers, and Shifting Liquidity
item.dc:creator: Evan Campbell, CFA
item.description: Life insurers have tilted away from Treasuries into structured and private credit, propelled by private equity ownership and NAIC treatment. Those flows are repricing markets, consistent with inelastic markets research that small, persistent allocations move prices. Record CLO issuance shows the shift; First Brands’ bankruptcy flags underwriting risk. The next test arrives as rules tighten in 2026.

item.title: The Insurance Capital Capacity Engine: the Cylinders that Powered Growth
item.dc:creator: Evan Campbell, CFA
item.description: PE-linked insurers now run a four-cylinder capacity engine: asset-intensive reinsurance lowers required capital; tax positioning lifts retained earnings; evolving solvency rules reshape charges on private assets; and short-horizon balance sheet funding via funding agreements and FHLB advances converts claims-paying strength into deployable cash. Together these steps explain the post-2019 surge in insurer deployable capital.

item.title: Why This Plumbing Was Built
item.dc:creator: Evan Campbell, CFA
item.description: Credit has migrated from banks to private platforms, and the centre of gravity has moved with it. Insurers, through asset-intensive reinsurance, are releasing capital and shaping who is financed, on what terms, and when liquidity turns. The same channel that supplies credit in calm periods can amplify stress when cushions shrink. We map how this transmission affects pricing, liquidity, funding terms, and exits across markets.

item.title: Out of the Light

item.title: Summer Series Part III: Transmission Lines — Private Credit and Insurance Balance Sheets
item.dc:creator: Evan Campbell, CFA
item.description: Private credit is recasting the circuitry of the financial system. In the final part of our Summer Series, we examine how insurance affiliates, NAV lines, and offshore reinsurance transmit stress. The system does not need to break to fail. Sometimes pressure just moves faster than recognition.

item.title: Summer Series Part II: Extend and Pretend, Again — A Behavioral History of Debt Deferral
item.dc:creator: Evan Campbell, CFA
item.description: "Extend and pretend" is not a post-GFC invention. It is a century-old instinct. In Part II of our Summer Series, we explore how debt deferral, maturity wall fears, and strategic inaction have repeated across cycles, from 1930s bank policy to 1990s Japan to today's CRE market. With historical quotes, visuals, and behavioral insight, we examine why delay often becomes the most rational path, until it no longer is.

item.title: Summer Series Part I: Lending Signals and the Repricing of Office Values
item.dc:creator: Evan Campbell, CFA
item.description: As capital markets recalibrate around sustainability and obsolescence risk, the office sector faces a stark financing divide. Modern, green assets are commanding tighter spreads and higher leverage, while legacy buildings are being priced out of the debt market entirely. In this analysis, we explore how lenders are redrawing the underwriting rulebook and what it means for the future of office real estate.

item.title: Research Review: ECB Study Quantifies Climate Risk Discounts in CRE
item.dc:creator: Evan Campbell, CFA
item.description: New ECB data shows climate risk is no longer a theoretical threat in commercial real estate. It’s being priced into asset values, liquidity, and investor behavior. From physical risk discounts to the premium on future-ready assets, the shift is reshaping capital flows across the eurozone.

item.title: Strategic Insight: Rethinking Underwriting — How Machine Learning is Reshaping CRE Modelling
item.dc:creator: Evan Campbell, CFA
item.description: Retrofitting is no longer a technical upgrade, it's a central investment decision. As regulatory pressure and ESG mandates reshape the market, traditional underwriting struggles to keep pace. This article explores how probabilistic modelling and machine learning offer investors a strategic edge, helping them navigate lease constraints, capital timing, and retrofit complexity with greater confidence.

item.title: Operational Strategy: The Quiet Legal Innovation Powering Europe’s Green Office Revolution
item.dc:creator: Evan Campbell, CFA
item.description: Green leases are emerging as powerful legal tools in Europe's push to decarbonize its office buildings. From retrofit cost-sharing to enforceable ESG clauses, these contracts are reshaping asset value and regulatory risk. Discover how a quiet legal evolution is driving a green office revolution, clause by clause.

item.title: Operational Strategy: The Retrofit Moment — Repricing, Regulation, and the Real Cost of Delay
item.dc:creator: Evan Campbell, CFA
item.description: Retrofitting is no longer just about compliance. As regulation tightens and tenant demand shifts, Europe's commercial real estate market is undergoing a decisive repricing. The opportunity now lies in identifying transition-ready assets before the market catches up.

item.description: As 2024 draws to a close, energy performance is moving from ESG checkbox to financial driver. Regulation, valuation standards, and early capital signals are converging to reprice inefficient assets across Europe. The efficiency reckoning has begun.
